hypothesis: Learned geometric pair scoring can improve formula-number ownership and rejection over nearest-rectangle distance on unseen original synthetic layout families.
scope: Relationship isolation only: source-authored oracle formula boxes and numeric-token candidates. No detector, PDF extraction, k2, rendering or real-paper generalization claim.
data_license: Original geometry and annotations, repository AGPL-3.0; no third-party paper content.
candidate_generation: All formula objects on page. Source-parent IDs, template names, text and source order excluded from features. Candidate recall measured separately.

model.type: class-balanced L2 binary logistic pair classifier
model.training: full batch deterministic float64; training-only normalization

comparator: Nearest rectangle: Euclidean bbox gap divided by numeric-token height; confidence exp(-gap/4).
calibration: Each method separately selects score threshold [0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9,0.95,0.98,0.99] and winner margin [0,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.3], maximizing correct accepted links with <=1% observed wrong-owner/accepted and >=100 accepted. No eligible setting means reject all. Test labels never select settings.
success_gate: Unseen-family correct accepted/true links improves >=5pp over calibrated comparator, with observed wrong-owner/accepted <=1%, true-link coverage >=50%, inference <50ms/page, model <10KiB. Synthetic mechanism gate only; report uncertainty.
stop: One frozen run; no output-informed parameter/feature/model changes. Existing paper diagnostics excluded. Temporary artifacts backed up before further work.
